Hey, Alex. A competitor just ordered my
new product on Amazon. The business is a billion-dollar company, and in the
shipping address, the person is someone whose job title is like new product
development. I feel like they're going to try and copy and steal my product.
What would you do about this in the long term?
>> First off, congratulations. The fact that anybody is copying you means that
you have something worth copying. In the game of business, you have small players
and big players, and David and Goliath have different advantages. The advantage
that you have is that you're scrappier, you're more nimble, you can make faster
decisions, you don't have approvals and boards, and innovation always comes from
the smallest players. And the ones who become disruptors are the ones that can
take that edge and lean into it. Maybe new marketing, new distribution, better
customer service. You win on some edge. The Goliath is going to take longer to
do things. They're going to have more resources than you, and they might
already have bigger distribution, maybe a brand or reputation. And so, you just
have to see this as you getting your your ticket punched on a mile marker
towards the ultimate goal that you have, and not that anything is wrong has
happened, or woe is me, or I'm a victim. Now it's time to go hard and win.
